findings.title: Used recovery codes in user storage are never consumed or removed
findings.body:
The credential is now resolved from user storage first. But the follow-up logic still assumes local storage. `allCodesUsed()` is evaluated on a model that user storage keeps as a plain list of raw codes. The only cleanup path is `removeStoredCredentialById`, which touches only local credentials, and the federated model may have no id. As a result:
- Nothing records which code was used, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` can keep asking for the same code.
- An exhausted set is never removed.
- `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` is never re-triggered after exhaustion.

The feature only creates and validates the federated credential. It does not implement the one-time-use semantics that recovery codes require.

findings.title: Test storage accepts any stored code, so the test cannot catch wrong-code or used-code handling
findings.body: `isValid` for recovery codes returns true if the input matches any stored code, and never marks codes as used. The login form asks for a specific code number, and the real provider validates only that code and consumes it. The new test enters only code 0, so it cannot detect reuse of a code or acceptance of the wrong code. This gap also hides the missing consumption logic in the authenticator.

findings.title: getCredentials can throw NPE when the user is unknown to the storage
findings.body: `getMyUser(user)` may return null, for example after the user was removed. `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp` without a null check. Other methods such as `isConfiguredFor` and `isValid` do check for null. Since `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now calls `getFederatedCredentialsStream` on every lookup, this NPE becomes reachable in more flows.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes are sent unhashed to user storage and the user label is dropped
findings.body: For user storage, the raw plaintext codes are serialized as JSON and passed via `updateCredential`. The local path stores hashed codes. This differs from the local behaviour, and the storage provider becomes responsible for protecting the secrets. The user label and creation time from `credentialModel` are not passed along, so they are lost for federated credentials. This should be documented, or the metadata should be passed through.
